chunks: Abu al-Hasan ibn Abi Jayd al-Qummi informed me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I saw Aba Abdillah عليه السلام place his hands before his knees when he performed sajdah.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Aba Abdillah, a title of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.رُكْبَتَيْهِ: his two knees, used here as the comparison point in movement into sajdah
key_terms.سَجَدَ: performed sajdah, meaning entered into prostration in salat
key_terms.يَدَيْهِ: his two hands, referring to the hands being placed on the ground first

ai.seo_question: When going into sajdah, should the hands be placed before the knees?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the practice of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام when going into sajdah. It indicates the manner of descending for prostration, specifically that the hands are placed before the knees, and is relevant to rulings of salat.
